name.evidence: Board decree stamped p61: land 'known by the name of Punta de Reys, situated in Marin County'; opinion heading p59: 'For the place called Punta de Reyes in Marin County containing two leagues of Land in a square'. year.evidence: Board decree p61: 'being the same land granted to Jose Francisco Snook by Governor Alvarado on the 8th day of June 1839'. governor.evidence: Board decree p61: 'granted to Jose Francisco Snook by Governor Alvarado on the 8th day of June 1839'. (Note: paired with the register's 1836/Berry this is impossible - the 1836 Berry grant was by Gutierrez, petition p5. Alvarado is right only for the confirmed 1839 Snook grant)

grantee.evidence: Board decree p61: the confirmed land is 'the same land granted to Jose Francisco Snook by Governor Alvarado on the 8th day of June 1839'. Berry (register's grantee) was the 1836 grantee of the surrounding tract who expressly released these 2 leagues to Snook (petition p5, p8-9); title chain confirmed: Snook -> Osio (28 Sept 1839) -> Randall (8 Jan 1852) (opinion p59)

name.evidence: Red label (image 1): 'PART of SAN ANTONIO GRANT / DOMINGO PERALTA AND VINCENTE PERALTA CLAIMANT'; DC caption stamped p.209: 'Vicente & Domingo Peralta vs The United States'. Register 'San Antonio (V. And D. Peralta)' matches.

year.evidence: Sola's decree, Mision de la Soledad 3 Agosto 1820 (stamped p.16), ordering possession to Sgt. Luis Peralta; juridical possession at San Leandro 16 Agosto 1820 (p.18); petitions in Nos. 273/274 (stamped pp.191, 200): land 'was on the third day of August in the year 1820... granted to... the late Don Luis Peralta... by the then Governor of California Don Pablo Vicente de Sola'.

governor.evidence: All three register governors appear as granting/confirming authorities in the file: Sola's 1820 concession (stamped pp.16-22, incl. his 18 Oct 1822 justificante); the Board opinion (stamped pp.181, 184) rests the claim on 'the grant of Gov Sola and the Concession and Order of Survey of Gov. Arguello' ('the land was restored to Peralta by the Decree of Arguello', p.181); Micheltorena's new title, Monterey 13 Feb 1844 (stamped pp.28-29): 'Expidase el titulo... Micheltorena' and decree declaring 'D. Luis Peralta dueno en propiedad del dicho terreno'.

grantee.evidence: Every grant instrument in the file runs to LUIS PERALTA, the father: Sola 1820 possession 'puse en posesion... al nombrado Luis Peralta' (stamped p.18); Micheltorena 13 Feb 1844 title declares 'D. Luis Peralta dueno en propiedad' (p.28); petitions pp.191/200: granted 1820 'to the father of this petitioner the late Don Luis Peralta'. Vicente and Domingo Peralta are the U.S.-era CLAIMANTS of the northern part (by their father's division and his will, exhibit M stamped pp.31-33), not the grantees. This is the dominant claimant-for-grantee error class.

land_case.evidence: Red label 'CASE No. 21 NORTHERN DISTRICT'; every stamped page reads '21 ND'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_nd021.pdf; DC caption p.209 'No 21 Being an appeal from the US board... in Case No 4 on the docket of said Board'.

outcome.evidence: Board opinion in Case No. 4, filed 7 Feb 1854 (stamped pp.180-187): 'the Claimants are entitled to a confirmation to the whole extent of the land claimed by them, from the Creek of San Leandro to the Arroyo... along the base of the Cerritos... of San Antonio or San Pablo'. But the claimants themselves appealed (notice of appeal 23 Mar 1854, stamped pp.207-208) and the transcript ends at p.217 with 1854 District Court depositions; NO District Court final decree is in this file. Commission confirmation verified; final confirmation and patent (register: Feb. 10, 1877) not in file (Phase C checks GLO).
